# Code-scanning alerts accepted after review.
#
# One `rule-id<TAB>path` per line. The CI `codescan` job fails on any open
# alert that is NOT listed here, so a new finding breaks the build while a
# reviewed one does not. Lines are matched on rule and file, never on line
# number, so ordinary edits do not silently re-arm or re-silence anything.
#
# GitHub code scanning does not honour `// codeql[rule-id]` comments in source,
# so this file is where an accepted alert is recorded and reviewed — in the
# repository, alongside the code, rather than in a web UI nobody opens.
#
# Adding a line here is a security decision. Say why, and keep it short.

# The proxy must fetch a URL; that is its function. The URL comes from
# netGuards.resolveUpstreamUrl(), which collapses leading slashes and returns
# null unless the resolved origin equals the backend's, so the request cannot
# leave wg-easy / AdGuard. Proven against a local listener before and after the
# fix, and on both production servers. CodeQL does not model the helper as a
# sanitizer. Regression tests: portal/test/net-guards.test.js.
js/request-forgery	portal/server.js

# The portal reads THIS host's own certificate on :443 to report its expiry,
# and that certificate is self-signed in the documented fallback — validating
# it would make the check impossible. Nothing is sent over those sockets and
# the peer is the local host. Two sites: /api/tls/cert and the security score.
js/disabling-certificate-validation	portal/server.js
